title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.

title: Left bundle branch area pacing induced dual bundle branches non-reentrant bigeminy and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy: a case report
authors: Chu Song-Yun; Yuxi Li; Li-Tong Qi; Er-dong Chen; Jing Zhou
abstract: A 76-year-old woman with intermittent advanced atrioventricular block from a previous left septal accessory pathway and atrioventricular (AV) nodal slow pathway ablation for supraventricular tachycardia was referred for pacing. Her echocardiogram showed no structural abnormality and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBaP) was achieved successfully, although frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) were observed during the procedure. In the interrogation before discharge, asymptomatic ST-segment elevation on the precordial electrocardiogram (ECG) necessitated an emergent coronary angiography. No significant stenosis or spasm of coronary arteries was found, while left ventriculography revealed apical dyskinesis suggestive of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. On closer inspection, frequent monomorphic PVCs developed after each pacing beat and formed a regular bigeminy pattern, indicating rapid LBB stimulation, and the facilitated slow conduction along the adjacent bundle branches induced the dual ventricular response. The resultant frequent desynchronized ventricular activation may have contributed to the stress for cardiac decompensation. Beta blocker was titrated to alter the critical time period matched for the repetitive activation pattern and to suppress sympathetic tension. The bigeminy was eliminated ultimately, and repositioning of the lead was avoided. The ventricular wall motion and LVEF recovered within months. This case highlights the importance of close observation of electrocardiographic monitoring after pacing. Despite the potential benefits for future cardiac function and lower pro-arrhythmic effect than routine pacing modalities, LBBaP may still be associated with new-onset arrhythmia and myocardial injury considering the baseline impairment of the electrical or anatomical substrate. Individualized management should be tailored according to specific scenarios.

title: Sphingolipid-Driven Lipotoxicity Promotes Calcific Aortic Valve Disease Through ER-Stress-NF-κB-EndMT Signaling and Is Therapeutically Targetable Through Serine Palmitoyltransferase Inhibition
authors: Elias Rawish; Timo Rusack; Peter Ruben Letsch; Julica Inderhees; Kristian Haendler; Carolin Gragoll; Jakob Christoph Voran; Michael Schneider; Katharina Kurz; Mohammed Rabiul Hosen; Maren Behrensen; Svenja Denker; Axel Kuenstner; Thorben Sauer; Jorge Duque-Escobar; Tobias Schmidt; Derk Frank; Thomas Stiermaier; Walter Raasch; Oliver J. Müller; Tanja Zeller; Hauke Stephan Busch; Timo Gemoll; Christoph Knosalla; Malte Spielmann; Zouhair Aherrharou; Scott Andrew Summers; Ingo Eitel; Christian Frerker
abstract: Background: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) lacks disease‑modifying therapy. LDL‑cholesterol lowering does not attenuate valvular calcification, suggesting cholesterol‑independent drivers. Thus, we tested whether ceramide accumulation drives CAVD and whether inhibiting sphingolipid de novo synthesis is therapeutic. Methods: We integrated lipidomics and proteomics of calcified and non-calcified human aortic valves with matched plasma. Mechanistic effects of ceramides were tested in primary human valvular interstitial cells (VICs). Therapeutic efficacy of serine palmitoyltransferase (SPT) inhibition with Myriocin was evaluated in ApoE−/− mice with PCSK9DY‑AAV-driven hyperlipidemia on Western diet using preventive treatment and therapeutic initiation after echocardiographically verified gradient elevation. Myriocin was additionally tested in a normolipidemic wild-type aortic valve wire-injury model. Hemodynamics, valve structure, lipid composition, and cell-state transitions were assessed by echocardiography, histology, lipidomics, and single-cell RNA sequencing. Results: Calcified human valves showed enrichment of long-chain ceramides linked to NF-κB, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT), and ER-stress/unfolded protein response (UPR) programs, whereas matched plasma sphingolipids were not elevated. In hVICs, long-chain C18 ceramide induced GRP78/BiP, CHOP, and ATF4, activated NF-κB, and promoted dose-dependent calcification. In vivo, SPT inhibition with Myriocin lowered valvular ceramides, reduced leaflet inflammation and mineralization, and improved cusp separation and transvalvular hemodynamics without lowering plasma LDL-cholesterol. In a therapeutic protocol initiated after gradient elevation, Myriocin halted further hemodynamic progression, providing the first evidence that de novo sphingolipid synthesis can be targeted after established CAVD onset in vivo. Myriocin also attenuated injury-induced stenosis in normolipidemic mice. Single-cell RNA sequencing showed reduced NF-κB/EndMT and ER-stress signatures and shifted VIC states away from osteogenic phenotypes. Conclusions: Human valve lipidomics and human VIC experiments identify ceramide-driven lipotoxicity as a driver of an ER-stress-NF-κB-EndMT axis in CAVD. In vivo, de novo sphingolipid synthesis is an actionable, LDL-independent target capable of modifying established hemodynamic disease progression, supporting SPT inhibition as a tractable strategy for medical CAVD therapy.

title: Phosphoproteomics profiling of the monocytes uncovers the mechanosensory pathways regulating monocytes responses to pathologic level of shear stress
authors: Austin Lai Lai; Chanly Chheang; Haoyun Fang; Habiba Danish; Yasmin Mirzaalikhan; Nalin Dayawansa; Anna M.D. Watson; Jonathan Noonan; Ching-Seng Ang; David Greening; Karlheinz Peter; Sara Baratchi
abstract: Background: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is the most common valvular heart disease in older adults and currently has no approved pharmacological therapy to prevent or slow disease progression. Aortic valve replacement, either surgically or by transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), therefore remains the only effective treatment for severe CAVD. Monocytes play an important role in driving inflammation and disease progression in CAVD. As the disease progresses and the aortic valve becomes increasingly stenotic, circulating monocytes passing through the narrowed valve are repeatedly exposed to pathological haemodynamic forces, including markedly elevated shear stress, before their recruitment into the valve tissue. However, how exposure to these mechanical forces reprograms circulating monocytes influences their subsequent responses within the valve remain poorly understood. Methods and Results: In this study, we used an engineered model of aortic valve stenosis combined with phosphoproteomic profiling to investigate how prolonged exposure to pathological shear stress reprograms circulating monocytes and influences their subsequent phenotype and function following recruitment into the valve matrix. We further used TAVI as a unique clinical model to determine whether restoration of physiological haemodynamics in patients with severe aortic stenosis reverses the shear-induced monocyte phenotype observed in our experimental model. We found that prolonged exposure of monocytes to pathological shear stress induced extensive remodelling of the proteomic and phosphoproteomic landscape, with enrichment of pathways associated with cellular metabolism, cytoskeletal organisation, and inflammatory signalling. Kinase activity analysis further identified increased protein kinase C (PKC) activity accompanied by suppression of AKT signalling. Consistent with these molecular changes, pathological shear stress increased actin polymerisation, mitochondrial membrane potential, intracellular calcium signalling, and PKC activity. Using a bioengineered extracellular matrix model that recapitulates the glycosaminoglycan-rich microenvironment of the stenotic aortic valve we found that prior exposure to pathological shear stress altered monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation, reducing oxidised LDL uptake and foam-cell formation while promoting co-expression of CD80 and CD163, indicative of a mixed macrophage phenotype. Finally, using a myeloid-specific Piezo1 knockout mouse model, we identified Piezo1 as a key mechanosensor linking pathological shear stress to PKC activation, mitochondrial responses, and persistent changes in monocyte phenotype following migration into the extracellular matrix. Conclusions: These findings establish a mechanistic link between abnormal valve haemodynamics, metabolic and inflammatory reprogramming of circulating monocytes, extracellular matrix remodelling, and immune dysregulation during CAVD progression, highlighting monocyte mechanotransduction and downstream PKC/Piezo1 signalling as potential therapeutic targets.

title: Association between radiotherapy laterality and cardiovascular disease mortality in male breast cancer patients receiving postoperative radiotherapy: a competing risks analysis and standardized mortality ratio assessment using SEER data
authors: Jia Si; Yufeng Zhang; Jianfei Jin; Fang Su
abstract: Background The association between radiotherapy (RT) laterality and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality in male breast cancer (MBC) remains unknown. We evaluated whether left-sided RT confers higher CVD mortality than right-sided RT in MBC patients, and quantified excess CVD mortality relative to the general U.S. male population. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 2,152 MBC patients receiving postoperative RT from the SEER database (2000–2020). Fine-Gray competing risks regression estimated subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs) for CVD death comparing left- vs. right-sided RT. Multiple sensitivity analyses were performed, including propensity score matching (PSM). Standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) were calculated using age-specific CVD mortality rates from CDC WONDER. Results Over a median follow-up of 5.6 years, no significant difference in CVD mortality was observed between left- and right-sided RT (fully adjusted sHR = 1.03; 95% CI: 0.71–1.49; P = 0.887). Results remained consistent across all sensitivity analyses (all P > 0.750). Compared with the general U.S. male population, irradiated MBC patients had a significantly elevated risk of CVD death (SMR = 1.36; 95% CI: 1.15–1.61). Age-stratified analysis showed the numerically highest point estimate in the 45–54 age group (SMR = 2.08; 95% CI: 0.84–4.29), though this did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions In MBC patients receiving modern RT, left- and right-sided treatment confer comparable risks of CVD mortality. Nevertheless, overall CVD mortality remains significantly higher than in the general U.S. male population, warranting comprehensive cardiovascular risk assessment and management for all RT recipients.

title: Aortic valve replacement with or without concomitant septal myectomy in patients with aortic stenosis and asymmetric septal hypertrophy: a retrospective cohort study
authors: Alimujiang Awakeri; Tong Tan; Shuiyun Wang; Hao Cui; Changwei Ren; Yongqiang Lai
abstract: The optimal surgical strategy for patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) accompanied by asymmetric septal hypertrophy (ASH) remains controversial. This study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of concomitant septal myectomy performed at the time of aortic valve replacement in this population. Between January 2020 and December 2025, among 6449 consecutive patients who underwent aortic valve replacement, 39 met the inclusion criteria of severe AS with concomitant ASH (interventricular septal thickness ≥ 15 mm). 22 patients underwent concomitant septal myectomy with AVR, while 17 underwent isolated AVR. Baseline characteristics, perioperative outcomes, echocardiographic parameters, and mid-term follow-up results were compared between groups. Baseline clinical characteristics were largely comparable between groups, although patients in the myectomy with AVR group exhibited more severe preoperative left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) and a higher prevalence of moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation. Early postoperative echocardiography demonstrated significantly lower LVOT peak velocity and pressure gradient, as well as reduced interventricular septal thickness, in the myectomy with AVR group. Two early deaths occurred in the myectomy with AVR group. At a mean follow-up of 3.11 years, LVOT hemodynamics and prosthetic valve function remained satisfactory in both groups, while left ventricular end-diastolic and end-systolic dimensions were significantly smaller in the myectomy with AVR group. In patients with severe AS and concomitant ASH, both isolated AVR and AVR with concomitant septal myectomy are feasible surgical strategies in selected patients. Isolated AVR was associated with a marked early postoperative elevation in LVOTPG,, suggesting that relief of fixed valvular obstruction may unmask dynamic subvalvular obstruction. Concomitant myectomy eliminates this early hemodynamic vulnerability by directly relieving subvalvular obstruction, and may be particularly beneficial in patients with higher preoperative LVOTPG. This strategy should be performed at centers with established myectomy expertise, and larger prospective studies are needed to define optimal patient selection criteria.

title: Editorial: The interplay of lipoprotein(a), systemic inflammation, and dietary patterns in predicting cardiometabolic disease outcomes
authors: Keyang Zheng; Heng Zhang
abstract: Two studies directly illustrate the value of integra@ng Lp(a) with modifiable biological or dietary factors. In a prospec@ve cohort of 1,741 pa@ents with premature myocardial infarc@on, Wang et al. found that elevated Lp(a) (>50 mg/dL; HR 2.27) and homocysteine (>15 μmol/L; HR 1.60) were independently associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), while concurrent eleva@on of both conferred substan@ally greater risk (HR 3.57) (5). This addi@ve interac@on is clinically relevant because homocysteine, unlike largely gene@cally determined Lp(a), is a modifiable metabolite influenced by folate and B-vitamin status. These findings support a precision-preven@on framework in which a rela@vely fixed inherited risk marker is interpreted alongside a correctable nutri@onal-metabolic one, as reflected in the authors' proposed "50-15" dual-threshold strategy for risk stra@fica@on.A complementary UK Biobank study by Zhang paired Lp(a) with a modifiable behavioral exposure, tea consump@on (6). Among pa@ents with established coronary heart disease, tea intake showed a nonlinear associa@on with MACE, with the lowest risk at approximately three cups per day (HR 0.828 vs. non-consump@on). Lp(a) did not mediate this associa@on, whereas the combined Lp(a)-C-reac@ve protein (CRP) profile appeared to modify its magnitude (interac@on p = 0.050), with the strongest associa@on observed in individuals with low Lp(a) and elevated CRP and no apparent benefit when both biomarkers were high. This dis@nc@on is important because a dietary exposure may influence cardiovascular risk without directly altering Lp(a), and its effects may instead depend on the underlying lipid and inflammatory environment. Notably, Lp(a) was dichotomized here at 50 nmol/L but at 50 mg/dL by Wang et al.; such unit heterogeneity remains a prac@cal obstacle to comparing Lp(a) thresholds across studies.Other contribu@ons broaden the dietary and metabolic context beyond a single biomarkernutrient pairing. Yi et al. analyzed cross-sec@onal data from 2,134 U.S. adults (NHANES) and 1,974 Chinese adults (Urumqi), and found that higher unprocessed beef intake was associated with higher triglyceride levels, with hypertriglyceridemia risk increasing more sharply above approximately 100 g/day; Mendelian randomiza@on provided addi@onal support for a poten@al causal rela@onship (7). Cui et al., meanwhile, cau@oned against a simple "more is beper" interpreta@on of nutri@onal biomarkers. Among 364 adults with preserved ejec@on frac@on (179 hypertensive, 185 controls) undergoing cardiac magne@c resonance imaging, higher circula@ng DHA, EPA, and docosapentaenoic acid (DPA) levels were independently associated with impaired ler atrial and ventricular strain in the hypertensive group only, with sex-specific paperns more marked in women (8). Although the retrospec@ve design limits causal inference, these findings underscore the importance of dose, clinical context, fapy-acid subtype, background diet, and individual suscep@bility when evalua@ng nutrient-related effects.Composite lipid-and inflamma@on-related indices have shown prognos@c value in cardiovascular cohorts (9), and several studies in this collec@on apply them to new outcomes. Kahaer et al. iden@fied the uric acid-to-HDL cholesterol ra@o (UAHDL) as a poten@al marker of cardiometabolicbased chronic disease and incorporated it into a mul@variable risk model (10). Jiang et al. found that the non-HDL-to-HDL cholesterol ra@o (NHHR) was associated with incident caro@d plaque and exhibited a nonlinear papern in which risk rose steeply below an inflec@on point of approximately 4.1 and then plateaued (11). Deng et al. extended this integra@ve approach to the hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) index, which combines nutri@onal, immune, hematologic, and thrombo-inflammatory informa@on (12). Lower HALP was associated with higher mortality across the con@nuous metabolic syndrome spectrum, while the combina@on of high metabolic burden and low HALP iden@fied individuals at par@cularly elevated risk, although the incremental contribu@on of HALP to discrimina@on was small (ΔC ≈ 0.002). Together, these studies suggest that metabolic burden and systemic vulnerability represent complementary dimensions of cardiometabolic risk.Related studies extend this framework to diabetes and cerebrovascular disease. He et al. found that the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and the triglyceride-HDL-glucose-body index (TyHGB) outperformed both conven@onal anthropometric measures and other lipid-based indices in predic@ng incident type 2 diabetes (13). Huang et al. reported an associa@on between the body roundness index and prevalent stroke, although its incremental discriminatory value beyond established risk factors was modest (14). Wu et al., in a dual-center cohort of adults with moyamoya disease, iden@fied LDL cholesterol as an independent predictor of preopera@ve hemorrhagic risk and combined it with total cholesterol in a clinically oriented nomogram (15). Collec@vely, these findings illustrate both the promise and limita@ons of accessible biomarkerbased tools: rou@ne clinical measures can capture mul@dimensional risk, but sta@s@cal associa@ons or modest improvements in discrimina@on do not necessarily translate into meaningful clinical benefit.

title: Formononetin relieves chronic stress-related neointimal hyperplasia in mice by regulating HDAC6
authors: Shanqian Li; Wanhua Wu; Chaozhi Xu; Yue Huang; Guixian Wu; Hongyu Ding; Zongyi Zhang; Yulin Zhang; Meimei Zheng; Hongxian Wu; Lina Hu
abstract: Introduction Chronic stress severely impairs physical and mental health and is a critical risk factor for cardiovascular diseases. Formononetin (FMN) has shown promising cardiovascular protective effects, yet its functional role and molecular mechanism in chronic stress-triggered arterial neointimal hyperplasia and concomitant mood disturbances remain poorly elucidated. Methods Network pharmacology was used to predict the underlying mechanisms of FMN against cardiovascular disease-depression comorbidity. A dual mouse model recapitulating chronic stress and carotid artery injury was established for in vivo validation. Histological staining, behavioral tests, Western blotting, β -galactosidase staining, and in vitro VSMC assays were performed to assess the effects of FMN and the HDAC6 inhibitor TubA. Results Network pharmacology identified 111 overlapping targets, with functional enrichment and molecular docking revealing that FMN primarily regulates inflammation, apoptosis, and autophagy via binding to core hub proteins including HDAC6, Bcl-2, and AKT1. In vivo , chronic stress aggravated arterial intimal hyperplasia and aortic senescence, and induced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. FMN treatment notably improved emotional disorders, reduced HDAC6 expression, activated autophagy (increased LC3B/A ratio), inhibited apoptosis (elevated Bcl-2/Bax ratio), attenuated NLRP3 and IL-6 expression, and alleviated intimal thickening. The HDAC6 inhibitor TubA recapitulated the vascular protective effects of FMN. Discussion FMN attenuates chronic stress-induced vascular injury and emotional dysfunction via suppressing HDAC6 signaling to restore autophagy, inhibit inflammation, and reduce apoptosis. This study unveils the dual cardio-neuroprotective capacities of FMN and provides novel mechanistic insights for the treatment of chronic stress-related cardiocerebral comorbidities.

title: Comparison of virtual and true ECG-gated coronary CT angiography in patients with acute chest pain: a prospective cohort study
authors: Wenyan Wei; Lin Lu; Yan Wu; Qianye Fang; Yuankun Li; Junyue Zhou; Runmeng Li; Dan Han; T. Ke; Wen Zhao
abstract: Purpose To compare the clinical value of true electrocardiogram-gated and virtual electrocardiogram-gated coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), and to provide a reasonable and effective imaging strategy for patients with acute chest pain. Methods A total of 254 patients with acute chest pain and suspected coronary artery disease who underwent CCTA were prospectively enrolled. Patients were alternately assigned according to examination date to the virtual ECG-gated group ( n = 126), or the true ECG-gated group ( n = 128). Examination time and radiation dose were recorded. Objectiveand subjective image quality parameters were evaluated. Objective parameters included image background noise, CT values of the aorta and coronary artery branches, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). Subjective image quality was assessed using a 5-point scale. In patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography (ICA) within 30 days after CCTA, diagnostic agreement was evaluated using ICA as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was assessed at the vessel level using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, with the four major coronary arteries from each patient considered as the units of analysis. Results (1) The virtual ECG-gated group demonstrated significantly improved examination efficiency compared with the true ECG-gated group, with a shorter total examination time (2.83 ± 0.37 min vs. 4.15 ± 0.49 min, P < 0.001) and positioning time (0.89 ± 0.26 min vs. 2.03 ± 0.35 min, P < 0.001). However, the radiation dose was higher in the virtual ECG-gated group than in the true ECG-gated group (3.58 ± 0.69 mSv vs. 3.18 ± 0.54 mSv, P < 0.001). (2) Image quality analysis showed that the virtual ECG-gated group had lower image noise than the true ECG-gated group, as well as higher SNR and CNR values for the aorta and coronary artery branches (all P < 0.001). However, CT values and subjective image quality scores were comparable between the two groups (all P > 0.05). (3) In the ICA-validated subgroup, the virtual ECG-gated group showed a higher diagnostic agreement rate than the true ECG-gated group (92.00% vs. 85.58%), with corresponding vessel-level AUC values of 0.89 and 0.82, respectively. However, the virtual ECG-gated group was associated with a higher radiation dose than the true ECG-gated group (3.58 ± 0.69 mSv vs. 3.18 ± 0.54 mSv), representing a trade-off for achieving an ECG-independent acquisition strategy and maintaining diagnostic image quality. Conclusion Virtual ECG-gated CCTA can significantly improve examination efficiency while maintaining comparable image quality and diagnostic performance to true ECG-gated CCTA. Although this approach was associated with a modest increase in radiation dose, this represents a trade-off for reducing dependence on real-time ECG acquisition and simplifying the CCTA workflow. Therefore, virtual ECG-gated CCTA may serve as a feasible and efficient imaging strategy for selected patients with acute chest pain, particularly in clinical scenarios requiring rapid evaluation or simplified workflow.

title: Case Report: Concurrent ventricular septal defect, pulmonic stenosis, and intrapulmonary arteriovenous anastomoses in a Korean raccoon dog (Nyctereutes procyonoides koreensis)
authors: Seoyeon Kim; Myeongsu Kim; Jae-Ik Han; Kichang Lee; Yoon HaKyoung
abstract: A 3-month-old intact male Korean raccoon dog ( Nyctereutes procyonoides koreensis ) was rescued and admitted to the Jeonbuk Wildlife Rescue Center with lethargy, dehydration, and dermatologic lesions consistent with Sarcoptes scabiei infestation. Physical examination detected a grade IV/VI systolic murmur, and thoracic radiography revealed generalized cardiomegaly. Transthoracic echocardiography identified a perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) with left-to-right shunting. Although no distinct structural abnormalities of the pulmonic valve were observed, increased pulmonic flow velocity (3.87 m/s), mild pulmonic regurgitation (1.68 m/s), and post-stenotic dilation of the main pulmonary artery supported a diagnosis of pulmonic stenosis (PS). Agitated saline contrast echocardiography demonstrated intrapulmonary arteriovenous anastomoses (IPAVAs), with microbubbles appearing in the left heart after the fourth cardiac cycle; this shunting decreased following oxygen supplementation. Five weeks later, thoracic radiography demonstrated a reduction in cardiac silhouette size, although cardiomegaly persisted. Echocardiography demonstrated progression of the VSD to bidirectional shunting. Systolic doming of the pulmonic valve, together with increased pulmonic flow velocity (4.39 m/s) and pulmonic regurgitation velocity (2.07 m/s), indicated worsening PS. Repeat agitated saline contrast echocardiography revealed microbubbles in the left heart within four cardiac cycles and in the abdominal aorta, indicating a right-to-left shunt component consistent with bidirectional shunting. These findings were attenuated after oxygen supplementation. The Korean raccoon dog subsequently died during anesthetic induction for further diagnostic imaging. Postmortem examination confirmed a perimembranous VSD and type A valvular PS characterized by fused commissures, with concurrent right ventricular hypertrophy, dilation, and interventricular septal thickening. To our knowledge, this case report is the first to describe the concurrence of VSD, PS, and IPAVAs in a Korean raccoon dog. It suggests that progressive PS may contribute to reversal of shunting across a VSD.

title: Hybrid surgical thromboembolectomy and crossover endovascular revascularization for acute lower-limb ischemia in a patient with active ovarian cancer receiving a PARP inhibitor (fuzuloparib): a case report and literature review
authors: Yibiao Jiang; Gang Wang; Zhenbin Liu; Haoran Jiao; Bowen Wang
abstract: Acute limb ischemia (ALI) is both limb- and life-threatening, and represents a vascular emergency. Malignancy produces a systemic hypercoagulable state that predisposes to arterial as well as venous thrombosis, and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors—now central to maintenance therapy in ovarian cancer—have, in aggregate randomized data, been associated with only a borderline venous signal and no clearly demonstrated independent arterial signal. We report a 60-year-old woman with active high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma maintained on oral fuzuloparib who presented with Rutherford category IIa ALI of the right lower limb on a background of chronic bilateral atherosclerosis. Angiography demonstrated occlusion of the right common iliac–external iliac–common femoral–proximal superficial femoral segment with collateral reconstitution and, after dedicated cardiac evaluation (regular sinus rhythm on ECG, no arrhythmia on perioperative telemetry, normal transthoracic echocardiography without intracardiac thrombus or vegetation, and no critical carotid stenosis), no identifiable cardioembolic source. A single-stage hybrid procedure—open common femoral thromboembolectomy followed by contralateral (crossover) endovascular treatment of a residual flow-limiting dissection with overlapping self-expanding and balloon-expandable covered stents—restored inline flow and salvaged the limb; the retrieved material was submitted for histopathology, which demonstrated bland fibrin–platelet–red-cell thrombus with lines of Zahn and negative AE1/AE3 immunostaining, excluding tumour embolism. The patient was transitioned to therapeutic anticoagulation within a multidisciplinary framework, and at 3 months the limb remained viable with palpable distal pulses. This case illustrates cancer-associated arterial thrombosis superimposed on atherosclerosis—on a background that also included PARP-inhibitor exposure, whose independent contribution remains speculative—highlights a hybrid open–endovascular strategy for definitive single-setting revascularization, and underscores the importance of excluding a cardioembolic source and confirming thrombus nature histologically, while individualizing long-term anticoagulation that is necessarily extrapolated from cancer-associated venous thromboembolism evidence, with attention to drug–drug interactions, thrombocytopenia and bleeding risk.

title: Ocular and Visual Complications Following Cardiac Surgery: A Scoping Review
authors: Maria Georgiadou; Theofilos Kanavos; Effrosyni Birbas; Maria Marinakis; Nikolaos Tsaftaridis
abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac surgery carries a disproportionately elevated risk of perioperative ophthalmological complications compared with other surgical procedures. Despite growing recognition of ocular and visual complications in this setting, a comprehensive synthesis of their entire spectrum has been lacking. Objective To systematically identify, map, and characterize the full range of ocular and visual complications reported following cardiac surgery, including disorders affecting ophthalmic structures, ocular motility, or visual function. Methods This scoping review was conducted following the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported according to the PRISMA-ScR recommendations. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception through January 2025 for studies reporting ocular or visual complications directly associated with heart or great vessel surgery. Evidence was charted by complication type and synthesized descriptively. Results Our review included 115 studies, mostly case reports. The most frequently reported complications were ischemic optic neuropathy, retinal vascular occlusive disorders, cerebral visual impairment, pituitary apoplexy, midbrain ischemia, visual pseudohallucinations, Horner syndrome, endophthalmitis, supranuclear ocular motility disorders, and orbital hemorrhage. Less recognized potential complications included ocular hypotony, amaurosis fugax, chiasmal stroke, Miller Fisher syndrome, ocular ischemic syndrome, paracentral acute middle maculopathy, and retinal detachment. Based on case report data, patients were predominantly men and most often in their 6th or 7th decades of life, ischemic optic neuropathy accounted for the most events, and coronary artery bypass grafting was the most frequently implicated operation. Recurring perioperative associations with cardiopulmonary bypass, hemodynamic instability, embolic phenomena, anemia, and preexisting vascular comorbidities were observed across studies. Visual outcomes were variable, with many ischemic complications resulting in persistent deficits. Conclusions Ocular and visual complications after cardiac surgery constitute a broad, heterogeneous group of disorders that, albeit rare, may result in substantial morbidity. Clinical awareness, perioperative vigilance, and prompt multidisciplinary evaluation may facilitate early identification and timely management.

title: Homozygous LMNA (p.Arg216His) variant in an Ecuadorian patient with atrial flutter and high-grade atrioventricular block: a case report
authors: Santiago Cadena-Ullauri; Viviana A. Ruiz‐Pozo; Rafael Tamayo‐Trujillo; Patricia Guevara‐Ramírez; Elius Paz‐Cruz; Rita Ibarra-Castillo; José Luis Laso-Bayas; Paul Onofre-Ruiz; Alejandro Cabrera‐Andrade; Ana Karina Zambrano
abstract: Cardiac laminopathies caused by LMNA variants may present with conduction disease, atrial arrhythmias, and ventricular dysfunction, sometimes before overt ventricular dilation. We report a 42-year-old Ecuadorian man with recurrent syncope and progressive exertional dyspnea who developed atrial flutter with a markedly slow ventricular response, high-grade atrioventricular block, and severe bradycardia. Next-generation sequencing using the TruSight Cardio panel identified NM_170707.4( LMNA ):c.647G > A (p.Arg216His) in a homozygous state. Franklin by QIAGEN classified the variant as pathogenic under the ACMG/AMP framework, although ClinVar contains conflicting interpretations and variant-specific functional and segregation studies were unavailable. Genetic ancestry analysis showed 89% Native American, 8.5% European, and 2.5% African ancestry. To our knowledge, p.Arg216His has not previously been reported in the homozygous state, whereas prior cardiac reports have involved heterozygous or compound heterozygous carriers, highlighting the novelty of this case report. This case expands the clinical and genotypic spectrum associated with LMNA-related cardiac disease and highlights the value of integrating electrophysiological, imaging, genomic, and ancestry data in underrepresented populations.

title: Role of Computed Tomography in the evaluation of coronary artery disease: A prospective study
authors: Tanish Khandelwal; Dr. Mahendra Kumar Verma; Roshani Begam; S. R. Meena
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Ubiquitination regulation in coronary microcirculation dysfunction: focus on the endothelial cells
authors: Qingying Zhang; Tingting Wang; Siyu Wang; 陈玉善; Yiwen Sheng; Haodi Zhang; Yunhao Wang; Jin BoYuan; Hua ChengJun; Xinyi Han
abstract: Basic and clinical research on coronary microvascular disease (CMD) has spanned half a century. As a pathogenesis independent of epicardial coronary stenosis, CMD has become a major hotspot in cardiovascular medicine. Ubiquitination, a vital post-translational modification in eukaryotic cells, precisely regulates target proteins via the E1-E2-E3 enzymatic cascade and plays a critical role in cardiovascular homeostasis and pathophysiology. Recent evidence indicates that the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) is deeply involved in the development of CMD by modulating nitric oxide production, barrier function, and inflammatory signaling in coronary microvascular endothelial cells. This review summarizes recent advances in ubiquitination, elaborates its molecular mechanisms in regulating coronary microcirculation, and dissects its pathogenic roles in diabetes, hypertension, and myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (MIRI).We further discuss potential therapeutic strategies and translational challenges of targeting the ubiquitination pathway for CMD, including proteasome inhibitors, E3 ligase modulators, deubiquitinase agonists, and PROTACs, aiming to provide new insights for future research.

title: Duplex ultrasound as an initial imaging clue to spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection: A case report
authors: Chenchen Wu; Bingru Zheng; Jiashen Wu; Zhikai Xu; Yingzhe Wu; 王鹏辉; Qianqian Wu; Runming Zhong
abstract: Spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection is uncommon and is usually confirmed with computed tomography angiography (CTA). Duplex ultrasound may provide an initial clue when the lesion and its flow abnormalities are directly visualized. A 56-year-old woman with untreated hypertension presented with acute persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back. Color Doppler ultrasound at the celiac artery origin demonstrated an intimal flap separating the true and false lumens, with an adjacent hypoechoic component without detectable flow. Spectral Doppler sampling within the dissected segment showed a peak systolic velocity of 225 cm/s with spectral broadening. Initial CTA confirmed proximal celiac artery dissection. On short-interval repeat imaging, the maximum outer diameter at the same anatomic level increased from 8.8 mm to 9.7 mm, the true lumen became more compressed, and new false-lumen thrombosis appeared. Symptoms had not progressed; the decision to intervene was driven by imaging progression. False-lumen coil embolization and stent placement were performed. Follow-up CTA demonstrated a patent stent, preserved major branch perfusion, and no residual false-lumen opacification. In this patient, duplex ultrasound provided an initial imaging clue, whereas CTA confirmed the diagnosis, documented interval remodeling, and assessed the post-treatment anatomy.

title: Effects of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists on coronary microcirculation: a mini-review
authors: Yu Li; Zhenhong Zhang
abstract: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) serve as a foundational therapies in the management of heart failure, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease. Their primary therapeutic efficacy stems from the competitive antagonism of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), which mitigates pathological cascades such as endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and perivascular fibrosis. Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD)—a pivotal pathological driver across a spectrum of cardiovascular diseases—is defined by impaired vasodilation, heightened microvascular resistance, and diminished coronary flow reserve (CFR). Given that CMD is inextricably linked to dysregulated MR signaling, the restoration of microvascular function represents a key mechanism through which MRAs exert their cardioprotective effects. This review delineates the physiological mechanisms, diagnostic indicators, and generational evolution of MRAs in the context of coronary microcirculation. By synthesizing evidence from animal and clinical studies, this work clarifies the therapeutic utility of MRAs for microvascular protection and provides a comprehensive framework for understanding their pharmacological role in CMD research.

title: ECMO-facilitated adult non-cardiac surgery: a structured narrative review
authors: Thomas F. O’Shea; Elizabeth J Bashian; Sarah Y. Park; Rachel Carpenter; Jordan R. H. Hoffman; Michael T. Cain; Markus Kowalsky; Benjamin A. Abrams; Nathan Clendenen; Nicholas R. Teman; Barbara Wilkey
abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) has traditionally been used as rescue support for severe respiratory failure, cardiopulmonary failure, or perioperative cardiac surgical care, but its expanding perioperative role has enabled selected non-cardiac operations in patients otherwise considered too unstable for surgery. We performed a structured narrative review of reported ECMO-assisted adult non-cardiac surgery, focusing on airway, trauma, burn, vascular, and obstetric applications. Published case reports, case series, retrospective cohorts, database analyses, and relevant reviews were identified through structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, PubMed Central, and Google Scholar, supplemented by manual reference review. For this review, ECMO-assisted surgery included both planned or enabling ECMO initiated specifically to permit an operation and ECMO-supported surgery performed while a patient was already receiving ECMO for respiratory or circulatory failure. Airway and tracheobronchial surgery represented the most developed application, whereas trauma, burn, vascular, and obstetric reports more commonly described ECMO as rescue or stabilizing support that permitted necessary surgery to proceed. Across specialties, the published experience demonstrates technical feasibility in highly selected reported patients but is dominated by case reports and small observational series, with substantial publication and selection bias and few comparator populations. Multidisciplinary planning, individualized cannulation and anticoagulation strategies, hemorrhage preparedness, anesthetic planning, and postoperative critical care are central to safe implementation. The current literature should not be interpreted as establishing a survival or treatment-effectiveness benefit.

title: Neutrophil-derived oncostatin m contributes to endothelial cell dysfunction during Treponema denticola interaction
authors: Dayron M. Leyva Rodriguez; Michelle B. Visser
abstract: Periodontitis (PD) is a common chronic inflammatory condition and a risk factor for cardiovascular diseases (CVD), yet underlying linking mechanisms remain unclear. The cytokine Oncostatin M(OSM) is elevated in both PD and CVD and has emerged as a potential mediator linking oral inflammation to vascular dysfunction. Neutrophils represent a prominent source of OSM during PD and OSM production is elevated by the periodontal pathobiont Treponema denticola (Td). This study investigated the role of exogenous and neutrophil-derived OSM in endothelial cell (EC) dysfunction and the contribution of heterogenous oral Treponema species in OSM production. Human aortic endothelial cells (HAoEC) were used to evaluate the effects of exogenous purified OSM and neutrophil-derived OSM on endothelial cell function. Endothelial permeability, neutrophil transmigration, cytokine production, cell activation and junctional integrity were assessed using transwell assays, ELISA, real-time PCR, immunoblotting and immunofluorescence microscopy. Exogenous OSM significantly increased HAoEC permeability, neutrophil transmigration and promoted endothelial activation; characterized by increased E-selectin, ICAM-1 and IL-6 expression. Mechanistically, OSM activated OSMR-STAT3 signaling and altered organization of VE-cadherin in adherens junctions and decreased expression of occludin in tight-junctions. Heterogeneous oral Treponema species promote OSM transcription and production from mouse and human neutrophils in vitro and in vivo using a mouse air pouch model of infection. T. denticola most robustly induced OSM release, likely independent of prominent virulence factors dentilisin and Msp. Co-culture model experiments revealed conditioned media from T. denticola -stimulated neutrophils promoted endothelial cell permeability and IL-6 while reducing endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) production. These effects were abolished by antibody neutralization of OSM, supporting a casual role of neutrophil-derived OSM. Overall, these findings provide mechanistic insight into putative links between PD and adverse cardiovascular events and identify OSM signaling as critical mediator in inflammation-driven endothelial dysfunction.

title: External validation of EuroSCORE II, additive EuroSCORE, and the STS predicted risk of mortality at 2,600 meters above sea level: a retrospective cohort study from a Latin American cardiac surgery centre
authors: David René Rodríguez Lima; Javier Darío Garzón-Rodríguez; Paula Liliana Torres-Gómez; Cristhian Rubio-Ramos; Leonardo Andrés Gómez-Cortes; Esther M. Campo-Bautista; Edith Eliana Rodriguez-Aparicio; Juan Diego Toro-Egas
abstract: Background EuroSCORE II, the Additive EuroSCORE, and the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS PROM) are widely used cardiac surgery risk models, but their performance has not been evaluated in a cardiac surgery centre located at high altitude (≥2,500 m asl). Methods We conducted a retrospective external validation study using prospectively collected registry data from consecutive adult cardiac surgery procedures performed at Hospital Universitario Mayor-Méderi (2,600 m asl), Bogotá, Colombia, between January 2019 and February 2026 ( N = 1,486). EuroSCORE II and the Additive EuroSCORE were calculated from the registry with the published models and evaluated in the full cohort; STS PROM was obtained from the official STS online calculator (2018 models) for the procedures within its scope ( n = 1,076). The outcome was in-hospital mortality. Discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and calibration with the observed to expected (O/E) ratio, calibration in the large, calibration slope, and calibration plots. Results In-hospital mortality was 7.9% (117/1,486), and 82.3% of procedures were non-elective. The AUC was 0.736 (95% CI 0.687 to 0.785) for EuroSCORE II, 0.733 (0.684 to 0.783) for the Additive EuroSCORE, and 0.815 (0.757 to 0.873) for STS PROM. All three models underestimated mortality: the O/E ratio was 2.50 (2.09 to 3.00) for EuroSCORE II, 1.50 (1.25 to 1.79) for the Additive EuroSCORE, and 2.72 (2.14 to 3.47) for STS PROM. Calibration slopes were 1.04 (0.82 to 1.26), 1.94 (1.46 to 2.41), and 1.31 (1.01 to 1.60), respectively. Underestimation was present across procedure types, risk strata, and calendar years, and persisted in sensitivity analyses of variable mapping and missing data (EuroSCORE II O/E 2.37 to 3.05). Conclusions In this high-altitude Colombian centre, EuroSCORE II, the Additive EuroSCORE, and STS PROM ranked patients acceptably, STS PROM best, but all underestimated in-hospital mortality, EuroSCORE II and STS PROM by more than twofold. The study design cannot separate an effect of altitude from differences in case mix, urgency, and local care. Local recalibration is needed before these models are used for counselling or benchmarking in this setting.

title: Clinical features of cough syncope: a systematic review
authors: Yanqin Fan; Meng Hou; 王海丽; Jingke Le; Liming Cao
abstract: Abstract Background Cough syncope (CS) is a rare subtype of syncope that remains underrepresented in evidence-based medicine. We aimed to characterize the clinical features of CS, with the aim of improving recognition and optimizing management strategies. Methods We present five cases of CS alongside a systematic review of its clinical characteristics based on published literature to improve recognition and optimize management. Reports of eligible patients were screened, and demographic, clinical, diagnostic, treatment, and outcome data were analyzed. Results This study included 60 patients with a mean age of 56 ± 15 years, 91% of whom were male. The most common underlying triggers were respiratory diseases, including pulmonary infections (35%) and bronchitis (22%). Common comorbidities included hypertension (26%), bronchial asthma (18%), and diabetes mellitus (15%). CS episodes were directly triggered by severe coughing in 93% (26/28) of patients. Episodes occurred at least twice daily in 20% of patients, and limb convulsions accompanied syncope in 22%. Symptoms improved after treatment in 98% of cases. After a median follow-up of 3.75 months (Interquartile Range: 2–12 months), the recurrence rate of syncope was 11%. CS, predominantly triggered by severe coughing, primarily affected middle-aged and older men. Conclusions CS predominantly affects middle-aged and older men and is frequently associated with pulmonary infections. Acute pulmonary infections serve as a common underlying trigger for CS, and patients are at risk of recurrent syncope and falls. Disease management should be focused on treating chronic airway disease, particularly chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

title: Ventricular arrhythmic burden before and after mitral valve repair in mitral valve prolapse: the role of mitral annular disjunction
authors: Ümeyir Savur; Berhan Keskin; Aysel Akhundova; Aykun Hakgör; Bilal Boztosun
abstract: Background Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) is increasingly recognized as an arrhythmogenic condition, with a subset of patients exhibiting ventricular arrhythmias beyond the hemodynamic effects of mitral regurgitation (MR). Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) has been proposed as a structural marker associated with arrhythmic risk, but its relationship with postoperative ventricular arrhythmias after mitral valve repair remains incompletely understood. We aimed to evaluate changes in ventricular arrhythmic burden following mitral valve repair and to investigate the association between preoperative MAD and postoperative ventricular ectopy. Methods This retrospective observational study included 77 patients with MVP who underwent surgical mitral valve repair for severe MR and had both preoperative and postoperative 24-h Holter recordings. Premature ventricular complex (PVC) burden and ventricular arrhythmias were assessed before and after surgery. MAD was evaluated retrospectively using transthoracic echocardiography. Multivariable linear regression, sensitivity analyses, and sequential model comparison were performed to evaluate the independent and incremental association of MAD with postoperative PVC burden. Results Overall PVC burden decreased significantly after mitral valve repair. Patients with preoperative MAD had a substantially higher PVC burden both before surgery [7,800 (7,000–9,575) vs. 4,200 (3,200–6,200) PVCs/24 h, p < 0.001] and after surgery [5,700 (5,175–6,425) vs. 2,200 (1,800–3,500) PVCs/24 h, p < 0.001] than those without MAD. The relative reduction in PVC burden was comparable between groups (−35.4 ± 20.6% vs. −39.5 ± 29.5%, p = 0.113). In multivariable analysis, preoperative MAD remained independently associated with higher postoperative PVC burden after adjustment for clinical covariates, prolapse phenotype, residual mitral regurgitation, and baseline PVC burden. Conclusions Mitral valve repair was associated with a significant reduction in ventricular ectopic burden in patients with MVP. However, preoperative MAD identified patients with a higher postoperative ventricular ectopic burden despite a similar proportional reduction in PVCs. These findings support the potential value of postoperative rhythm surveillance in patients with preoperative MAD.

title: Endothelial and oxidative biomarker profiles in atrial fibrillation according to SGLT2 inhibitor exposure: a cross-sectional study
authors: Łukasz Wołowiec; Joanna Banach; Michał Janiak; Agata Szymczak; Jacek Budzyński; Anna Wołowiec; Mariusz Kozakiewicz; Julia Warecka; Grzegorz Grześk

title: In-hospital events and resource utilization associated with percutaneous-based vs. open lumbar fusion, stratified by admission status: a national inpatient sample analysis
authors: Hao Yang; Jianlong Li; Yu Sun
abstract: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) may be associated with a more favorable short-term inpatient profile after lumbar fusion, but whether these associations differ by admission status remains unclear. In this retrospective observational analysis of repeated cross-sectional 2016–2022 National Inpatient Sample (NIS) discharge data, hospitalizations of adults undergoing lumbar fusion were identified and stratified as elective or non-elective. The exposure was defined by the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Procedure Coding System-coded approach as percutaneous-based (percutaneous/percutaneous-endoscopic) vs. open fusion. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression accounted for the NIS’s complex design and adjusted for demographics, hospital characteristics, fusion extent, indication/case-mix, and individual Elixhauser comorbidities; formal approach-by-admission interactions were tested. A total of 174,704 hospitalizations met the inclusion criteria. In elective admissions, percutaneous-based fusion was associated with lower odds of blood product transfusion (aOR 0.448, 95% CI 0.311–0.644), acute posthemorrhagic anemia (aOR 0.591, 95% CI 0.475–0.736), and prolonged length of stay (aOR 0.774, 95% CI 0.656–0.914). In non-elective admissions, it was associated with lower odds of acute posthemorrhagic anemia (aOR 0.669, 95% CI 0.491–0.912) and non-home discharge (aOR 0.666, 95% CI 0.502–0.883). Significant approach-by-admission interactions were observed for blood product transfusion ( P = 0.037) and non-home discharge ( P = 0.022). These findings indicate that the short-term association profile of percutaneous-based vs. open lumbar fusion differs across admission settings and specific in-hospital measures.

title: Diagnostic yield of 24-hour Holter monitoring in children presenting with chest pain, palpitations, or syncope: A single-center retrospective study
authors: Aslı Urunca; Bihter Karabacak; Serhat Koca; Hazım Alper Gürsu; Ayşe Esin Kibar Gül
abstract: Objective: The aims of this study were to evaluate the diagnostic yield of 24-hour Holter monitoring (HM) in children referred for chest pain, palpitations, and/or syncope, to identify independent predictors of clinically significant dysrhythmia and of the need for clinical intervention, and to assess the value of repeat HM. Materials and Methods: Single-center retrospective study of 584 patients aged 6–18 years who underwent 24-hour HM between February 2023 and February 2024, grouped by presenting symptom (isolated palpitations, isolated chest pain, isolated syncope, or combined [≥2 symptoms]). HM findings were classified as normal, clinically non-significant arrhythmia, or severe dysrhythmia. Independent predictors were assessed by multivariable Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression. Results: Mean age was 13.4 years; 64.6% were female. HM was normal in 83.4%, non-significant in 12.7%, severe in 3.9%. Findings differed across groups (p=0.007; only chest pain vs syncope, p=0.002). No isolated syncope patient had a severe dysrhythmia or required intervention (0/108). Intervention was most frequent in isolated chest pain (13.2%), but 7 of 12 were empirical beta-blockers for benign ectopy or normal HM. An abnormal ECG was the only independent predictor of intervention (OR 6.78, 95% CI 3.15–14.29; p<0.001) and of severe dysrhythmia (OR 13.32, 95% CI 5.46–33.16; p<0.001); presenting symptom was not independently associated with either. Arrhythmia on the initial HM predicted later actionable arrhythmia (27.1% vs 2.3%). Of those with a normal initial HM, 10.2% underwent repeat HM and 12.0% showed a new finding. Family history of sudden death was not associated with severe dysrhythmia (p=0.406). Conclusion: The diagnostic yield of HM varies by presenting symptom, but this variation is explained by ECG findings rather than the symptom itself. Arrhythmia on the initial HM strongly predicts subsequent intervention. No patient with isolated syncope had a severe dysrhythmia, although the retrospective single-center design precludes a definitive exclusion of risk.

title: Quality of life in hyperkalemia: baseline analysis of a cohort study of management of hyperkalemia in patients with chronic kidney disease or heart failure in Japan
authors: Ken‐ei Sada; Hajime Yamazaki; Takafumi Wakita; Yosuke Yamamoto; Jui Wang; Yoshihiro Ônishi; Tadateru Hamada; Ryotaro Ide; Masayoshi TAKEDA; Shunichi Fukuhara; Yugo Shibagaki
abstract: Abstract Background Hyperkalemia is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and chronic heart failure (CHF), often leading to treatment dilemmas regarding renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors. Although potassium binders and dietary restrictions are central to chronic management, their quality-of-life (QOL) impact remains insufficiently described. This study aimed to characterize real-world treatment patterns and evaluate treatment impact on QOL. Methods We analyzed baseline data from a prospective cohort in Japanese nephrology and cardiology outpatient clinics. Participants were adults with CKD (≥ stage G3) or CHF (New York Heart Association class II-IV) who initiated potassium binders within 6 months. Clinical data, serum potassium values, and patient-reported outcomes (generic QOL, disease/treatment-specific QOL, and adherence measures) were obtained at enrollment. Results Among 347 patients, the median age was 75 years, and 74% were male; 93% had CKD. At enrollment, 59% were prescribed a RAAS inhibitor. Dietary therapy was implemented in 29%. Physical scores of generic QOL were lower than population norms, whereas mental scores were comparable. Treatment-specific QOL scores suggested that potassium binders may have had a relatively small impact on QOL compared with dietary therapy. Adherence to potassium binders was high. Conclusions Concurrent use of RAAS inhibitors and potassium binders was common, consistent with a role for binders in supporting RAAS inhibitor continuation. Potassium binders showed little perceived impact, indicating that pharmacologic potassium control may be acceptable to patients managing multiple lifestyle limitations. Study registration. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05297409).

title: Association of dietary antioxidant patterns with heart failure risk in patients with hypertension
authors: Xingwan Bai; Zhenzhen Wu; Yun Zhao; Youbo Xu; Nei Li; Lexiang Shi; Gao Xue; Hexiang Yang; Lei Zhao; Dawei Liu
abstract: Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for heart failure (HF) and contributes substantially to the cardiovascular disease burden in China. Oxidative stress and redox imbalance have been implicated in the progression from hypertension to HF. The composite dietary antioxidant index (CDAI) has been associated with favorable cardiovascular outcomes; however, evidence regarding its association, particularly the potential nonlinear dose–response relationship, with HF among patients with hypertension remains limited. To investigate the association between CDAI and HF among patients with hypertension and to characterize the dose–response relationship and the relative contributions of the individual antioxidant nutrients included in the CDAI. A total of 1,156 patients with hypertension were included in this study and classified into the HF group ( n = 48) or non-HF group ( n = 1,108) based on the occurrence of HF. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated food-frequency questionnaire, and the CDAI was calculated from seven antioxidant nutrients. Associations between CDAI and HF were evaluated using Firth penalized logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses. Weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression was used to assess the joint association of the antioxidant nutrient mixture with HF and to estimate the relative contribution of each nutrient. Higher CDAI levels were associated with lower odds of HF. In the fully adjusted Firth penalized logistic regression model, compared with participants in the lowest CDAI tertile, the odds ratios were 0.39 (95% CI, 0.17–0.82; P = 0.013) for the second tertile and 0.21 (95% CI, 0.08–0.54; P < 0.001) for the highest tertile. RCS analysis indicated a significant nonlinear inverse association between CDAI and HF. WQS regression showed that the combined antioxidant nutrient mixture was inversely associated with HF, with total carotenoids and zinc contributing the greatest weights to the mixture index. Higher CDAI levels were associated with lower odds of HF among patients with hypertension, with evidence of a nonlinear dose–response relationship. The combined intake of the seven antioxidant nutrients was also inversely associated with HF, with total carotenoids and zinc making the largest relative contributions. Optimizing dietary antioxidant intake may represent a potential strategy associated with lower HF risk among individuals with hypertension.
